Vector Search Service Example

Vector searches through the database object server over mutual TLS: VECTOR_INFO, VECTOR_SEARCH and a day range.

Contents

What It Shows
Running It
Sample Output
Source

What It Shows

The database object server (gxdbobject.h) answers two vector requests on a database whose config names its vectors (vectors = notes.vixset, a manifest or one .vix file):

  • VECTOR_INFO (op 8): the dimension, element type, metric, number of files, nodes and spec.
  • VECTOR_SEARCH (op 7): the k nearest to a query, with an optional tag filter and day range. The server skips files outside the range from the manifest; every result names its file. At most a few searches run at a time (SetVectorLimits()); vector requests never take the database's own lock, and a replicated copy's vectors are searched under its apply lock.

The program has three modes: make (three day files and their manifest), serve (the server, read only) and search (the client). Its comment gives the request and reply layouts. Linux and Windows, like the object server.

Running It

examples/oodb/vector_search_walkthrough.sh BUILD/examples

The walkthrough makes throwaway certificates (the openssl command), the data, starts the server on 127.0.0.1 and runs the client twice: every day, then one day (the other two files skipped). Exit code 0 when every check passes; KEEP=1 keeps its folder.
